breakfast.name: Saltfish and Dumplings
instructions: Boil and flake saltfish
Sauté with onion, tomato, pepper, thyme
Make dumplings, boil
Serve together

breakfast.name: Johnny Cakes
instructions: Mix dough
Shape into rounds
Deep fry until golden

breakfast.name: Corn Porridge
instructions: Kittitian corn porridge is the traditional breakfast before modern cereals arrived
Cornmeal cooked slowly in coconut milk -- the coconut milk is essential
Sweetened with sugar and spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg
Stirred constantly to prevent lumps
Vanilla added at the end for fragrance
breakfast.description: Saint Kitts cornmeal porridge cooked in coconut milk with cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla. Sweetened, smooth, and fragrant. The traditional breakfast before imported cereals. Stirred constantly while cooking.

breakfast.name: Bread and Butter with Cocoa Tea
instructions: Cocoa tea is not hot chocolate -- it is brewed from raw local cacao sticks
The cacao sticks: raw cacao that is dried, fermented, and formed into sticks
Grated and boiled with cinnamon, bay leaf, and milk
The flavor is earthy, slightly bitter, chocolatey -- more complex than hot chocolate
Served with fresh bread and butter -- the traditional Kittitian breakfast
The bread from local bakeries: slightly sweet, soft rolls
breakfast.description: Kittitian raw cacao tea with bread -- cocoa sticks (dried, fermented local cacao) grated and boiled with cinnamon, bay leaf, and milk into a rich earthy chocolate-like brew. Served with fresh bread and butter. More complex and earthy than hot chocolate.

lunch.name: Stewed Saltfish with Spicy Plantains
instructions: Soak and flake salt cod
Make tomato-onion sauce, add fish
Fry plantain slices
Serve together

lunch.name: Pelau (One-Pot Rice)
instructions: Brown chicken with sugar
Add onion, garlic, thyme
Add rice, peas, coconut milk
Cook covered
lunch.description: One-pot rice with chicken and pigeon peas.

lunch.name: Conch Fritters
instructions: Conch fritters are the Caribbean staple -- conch meat in a seasoned batter
The conch must be tenderized first -- it is naturally tough
Tenderized by pounding or grinding to break the muscle fibers
Minced conch folded into a seasoned batter with aromatics
Dropped by spoonful into hot oil and fried until golden
Served with a Scotch bonnet aioli or lime dipping sauce
lunch.description: Caribbean conch fritters -- tenderized and minced conch folded into seasoned batter with onion, celery, and Scotch bonnet, fried until golden. Served with lime or hot sauce. The conch must be pounded first to tenderize.

lunch.name: Rice and Peas with Stewed Chicken
instructions: Rice and peas is the Caribbean Sunday dish -- rice cooked with pigeon peas in coconut milk
The peas: pigeon peas (gungo peas) -- the Caribbean choice
Coconut milk gives the rice its characteristic creamy, slightly sweet flavor
Stewed chicken: browned with browning sauce, then braised with aromatics
The browning sauce: caramelized sugar -- gives the deep color
The combination of rice and peas + stewed chicken is the Caribbean Sunday plate
lunch.description: Kittitian Sunday rice cooked in coconut milk with pigeon peas, served alongside stewed chicken (browned with caramelized sugar browning sauce and braised with thyme and allspice). The coconut milk gives the rice its creamy, slightly sweet character. The regional Sunday dish.

lunch.name: Breadfruit Salad
instructions: Breadfruit arrived in the Caribbean by way of Captain Bligh and the Bounty mutiny
Captain Bligh transported breadfruit from Tahiti to the Caribbean as a cheap food for enslaved workers
The enslaved workers initially refused to eat it -- they associated it with their forced labor conditions
Over time breadfruit became central to Caribbean cuisine
Roasted breadfruit: the preferred preparation -- roasted over fire or in the oven
The roasted breadfruit has a potato-like interior and slightly smoky exterior
Made into a salad with fresh vegetables and a lime vinaigrette
lunch.description: Caribbean breadfruit salad -- breadfruit (roasted or boiled, potato-like texture) tossed with cucumber, tomato, and onion in lime vinaigrette. Breadfruit arrived via Captain Bligh from Tahiti as food for enslaved workers; it became central to Caribbean cuisine over time.

dinner.name: Goat Water (Goat Stew)
instructions: Brown goat meat
Add spices and water
Simmer 2 hours
Add breadfruit and dumplings last 30 min
dinner.description: Rich goat stew — St. Kitts's signature.

dinner.name: Curry Conch
instructions: Tenderize and dice conch
Sauté onion, garlic, curry
Add coconut milk and potatoes
Add conch, simmer 25 min

dinner.name: Steamed Red Snapper
instructions: Steamed red snapper is the Kittitian fish dish
The fish is scored to allow the marinade to penetrate
Marinated with lime, garlic, and Scotch bonnet
Steamed in a covered pan with aromatics
The steam creates a savory broth at the bottom of the pan
Served with the broth poured over -- the broth is the sauce
dinner.description: Saint Kitts steamed red snapper -- whole fish scored and marinated with lime, garlic, and Scotch bonnet, then steamed with tomatoes and aromatics. The steam creates a savory broth that serves as the sauce. Served with the liquid poured over.

dinner.name: Ducana and Saltfish
instructions: Ducana is the Kittitian steamed sweet potato dumpling -- wrapped in banana leaves
The sweet potato, coconut, and pumpkin are grated and mixed
Sweetened with sugar and spiced with cinnamon and vanilla
The mixture is placed in banana leaves and tied
Steamed until firm -- the banana leaves impart a subtle flavor
Traditionally served alongside saltfish as the savory counterpart
The sweet ducana and the salty fish: the Kittitian combination
dinner.description: Saint Kitts steamed sweet potato dumplings -- grated sweet potato, coconut, and pumpkin sweetened with sugar and cinnamon, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed until firm. The banana leaf imparts flavor. Traditionally served alongside saltfish: sweet ducana and salty fish is the Kittitian combination.

dinner.name: Stewed Pork with Dumplings
instructions: Stewed pork with dumplings is the hearty Kittitian home dinner
The pork is browned with browning sauce for the dark caramelized color
Braised low and slow with aromatics
The dumplings are added near the end -- they absorb the stew liquid
The dumplings are simple: just flour, water, and salt, rolled and dropped in
dinner.description: Kittitian stewed pork with boiled dumplings -- pork shoulder browned with browning sauce (caramelized sugar) and braised low and slow with thyme, garlic, and Scotch bonnet. Flour dumplings added near the end absorb the stew liquid.

snacks.name: Conkies (Cornmeal Pudding)
instructions: Mix ingredients
Wrap in banana leaves
Steam 45 min
snacks.description: Steamed cornmeal pudding in banana leaves.

snacks.name: Tamarind Balls
instructions: Tamarind balls are the Caribbean sweet-sour candy
The ripe tamarind pods are shelled and the pulp is worked by hand
Seeds are removed from the pulp
Sugar, salt, and a pinch of hot pepper are worked in
Rolled into balls by hand
The combination: sour tamarind, sweet sugar, salt, and heat -- all at once
snacks.description: Caribbean tamarind candy -- ripe tamarind pulp worked by hand with sugar, salt, and a pinch of hot pepper, rolled into balls. The flavor is sour, sweet, salty, and hot simultaneously. A beloved Caribbean sweet-snack.

snacks.name: Plantain Chips
instructions: Green plantain chips are the Caribbean snack
Green (unripe) plantains: starchy, not sweet -- they become crispy when fried
Sliced very thin on a mandoline or by knife
Fried in hot oil until golden and crispy
Salted immediately while hot -- the salt sticks better on the hot chips
snacks.description: Caribbean green plantain chips -- unripe (green, starchy) plantains sliced very thin and fried until golden and crispy. Salted while hot. Green plantains are starchy, not sweet, so they crisp up like potato chips.

snacks.name: Guava Cheese
instructions: Guava cheese (guava paste) is the Caribbean preserve candy
The guava is cooked with sugar until very thick
Poured into a flat pan and allowed to cool and set
The paste firms to a sliceable, dense candy consistency
Called guava cheese because of its firm, sliceable texture
Eaten plain as a sweet, or with cheese (the combination is traditional)
snacks.description: Caribbean guava paste candy -- ripe guava pulp cooked with equal weight sugar until very thick, poured flat and set to a firm, sliceable consistency. Called cheese for its texture. Eaten as a sweet or paired with actual cheese in the traditional combination.

desserts.name: Sugar Cake
instructions: Cook coconut and sugar until thick
Add ginger
Drop onto wax paper
Let harden

desserts.name: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
ingredients: Cake batter: flour, sugar, eggs, butter, baking powder
instructions: Pineapple upside-down cake is a Caribbean celebration cake
The pineapple is native to South America but became emblematic of the Caribbean
Brown sugar and butter are melted in the pan first -- forming the caramel layer
Pineapple rings are placed on the caramel layer
The cake batter is poured over and baked
When inverted, the caramelized pineapple is revealed on top
desserts.description: Caribbean pineapple upside-down cake -- caramelized brown sugar and butter with pineapple rings form the base, covered with vanilla cake batter, baked, then inverted to reveal the caramelized pineapple crown. A celebration cake.

imageCredit.author: Kimberly Vardeman from Lubbock, TX, USA

desserts.name: Coconut Ice Cream
instructions: Coconut ice cream is made by churning sweetened coconut milk
No-churn version: whipped condensed milk with coconut milk, frozen
The full-fat coconut milk provides a creamy base
The flavor: rich, tropical, slightly sweet
Fresh grated coconut adds texture if stirred in during freezing
desserts.description: Caribbean coconut ice cream -- sweetened full-fat coconut milk churned or no-churn frozen into rich, tropical ice cream. Fresh grated coconut adds texture. Simple and cooling.

drinks.name: Cane Sugar Juice
instructions: Press sugarcane through mill
Add lime juice
Serve over ice

drinks.name: Ting
instructions: Pour over ice
Refreshing Caribbean grapefruit soda

drinks.name: Mauby
ingredients: Mauby bark (dried bark of Colubrina elliptica)
instructions: Mauby is the Caribbean bitter-sweet herbal drink from tree bark
Mauby bark: the dried bark of Colubrina elliptica -- a Caribbean tree
Brewed by boiling the bark with spices
The flavor: initially bitter, then sweet -- an acquired taste
Every Caribbean island has its mauby tradition
Considered a digestive and a cooling drink
drinks.description: Caribbean mauby drink -- bark of Colubrina elliptica boiled with cinnamon, anise, bay leaf, and cloves into a bittersweet herbal brew, sweetened with sugar. The flavor starts bitter and finishes sweet. A Caribbean digestive and cooling drink.
